Fit an Approximate Bayesian Growth Curve Model

Source: R/inlavaan.R
agrowth.Rd

Fit an Approximate Bayesian Growth Curve Model

Usage

agrowth(
  model,
  data = NULL,
  dp = priors_for(),
  test = "standard",
  vb_correction = c("onestep", "full", "none"),
  n_qmc = NULL,
  vb_method = NULL,
  marginal_method = c("skewnorm", "gaussian"),
  marginal_correction = NULL,
  nsamp = 1000,
  samp_copula = NULL,
  samp_norta = NULL,
  cov_as_cor = FALSE,
  sn_fit_ngrid = NULL,
  sn_fit_logthresh = NULL,
  sn_fit_temp = NULL,
  sn_fit_sample = TRUE,
  control = list(),
  verbose = FALSE,
  debug = NULL,
  add_priors = NULL,
  optim_method = NULL,
  numerical_grad = NULL,
  hessian_method = NULL,
  cores = NULL,
  ppp_method = c("onestep", "em"),
  ppp_nsamp = 250L,
  marginal_scan = c("linear", "exact", "laplace", "plain"),
  silent = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

model

A description of the user-specified model. Typically, the model is described using the lavaan model syntax. See model.syntax for more information. Alternatively, a parameter table (e.g., the output of the lavParTable() function) is also accepted.

data

An optional data frame containing the observed variables used in the model. If some variables are declared as ordered factors, lavaan will treat them as ordinal variables.

dp

Default prior distributions for the different types of model parameters; a named character vector as returned by priors_for(). Types left out take their default priors. A name that is not a type, such as a misspelt one, gives a warning. dp = blavaan::dpriors() works too.

test

Character vector naming the post-estimation quantities to compute and store with the fit. The atoms are "ppp" (posterior predictive p-value), "dic" (deviance information criterion and its pD), "loo" (leave-one-out cross-validation, see loo()) and "waic" (see waic()). Three aliases stand for sets of atoms: "standard" (the default) and its synonym "default" give c("ppp", "dic"); "full" gives all four; "none" gives nothing. Aliases and atoms may be mixed and are unioned, so test = c("standard", "loo") adds the LOO to the default set. The LOO and the WAIC come from one Taylor pass, so asking for either stores both. They run only when asked for, with no time budget. On a model the casewise machinery does not support (PML or ordinal data, conditional.x = TRUE, multigroup two-level) they are skipped with a warning and the rest of the fit proceeds. For a two-level model the PPP follows blavaan: each of ppp_nsamp posterior draws generates replicate data, which are scored against the saturated model (see ppp_method). The two-level PPP is experimental. The fit records what was requested and what was computed (get_inlavaan_internal(fit, "test")); summary(), fitmeasures(), deviance(), logLik() and timing() report only what was computed. add_loo() stores the LOO and WAIC post hoc; loo() and waic() compute on demand. For a random-slope model "ppp" is dropped, with a warning when it was asked for and a message otherwise (see the Random slopes section of inlavaan()). "dic", "loo" and "waic" are unaffected.

vb_correction

The variational Bayes (VB) correction of the posterior mean of the Laplace approximation. "onestep" (default) takes one step from the mode and checks it. Where the check fails, the posterior is far from Gaussian along the step: the fit then solves the VB equation instead, and warns (see diagnostics()). "full" iterates the correction to its fixed point, and "none" leaves it out. The correction moves the marginal log-likelihood, the point at which the DIC is computed, the centre of the LOO and the WAIC, and the Gaussian marginals of marginal_method = "gaussian" and their draws. It does not move the skew-normal marginals or their draws, which are scanned from the mode.

n_qmc

Has no effect. The VB correction now takes a deterministic step, with no quasi-Monte Carlo nodes.

vb_method

Has no effect. The VB correction now has one rule, and vb_correction = "full" iterates it.

marginal_method

How the marginal posterior of each parameter is approximated. "skewnorm" (default) fits a skew-normal distribution to a scan of the log-posterior along the parameter (see marginal_scan). "gaussian" takes the Gaussian marginal of the Laplace approximation, centred at the VB mean, which is faster. The old values warn: "marggaus" is the old name of "gaussian", and "asymgaus" now runs "skewnorm". "sampling" is kept for a sampler that is under development, and gives an error.

marginal_correction

Use marginal_scan. "none" and FALSE are marginal_scan = "plain", which gives the same fit. "shortcut", "shortcut_fd" and "hessian" run marginal_scan = "linear".

nsamp

The number of samples to draw for all sampling-based approaches (including posterior sampling for model fit indices).

samp_copula

Has no effect. The draws always couple the fitted marginals by a Gaussian copula. With marginal_method = "gaussian" they are the draws of the Laplace approximation.

samp_norta

Has no effect. The draws no longer adjust the correlations of the copula.

cov_as_cor

Logical. Residual and latent-disturbance covariance parameters (~~ between two observed or two latent variables) are always estimated on the correlation scale internally (an atanh link, the same as for std.ov/std.lv-standardised parameters); by default their reported marginal is then re-derived on the covariance scale \(\sigma_i \sigma_j \rho\) from a posterior sample (see nsamp), because that is the scale lavaan/blavaan report by default. When TRUE, that re-derivation is skipped and each such parameter's own directly profiled correlation-scale marginal \(\rho \in (-1, 1)\) is reported instead – useful for comparing the profiling machinery (skew-normal fit, VB, ...) against a correlation-scale reference without the sampling/copula step in between. Model estimation is identical either way; only what is reported for these parameters changes. The returned parameter table keeps their covariance classes, so loo() and waic() after the fit score the same model, and the setting is stored as get_inlavaan_internal(fit)$cov_as_cor. The point estimates of these parameters are correlations, so methods that use the point estimates as model parameters (such as fitted() and residuals()) are not meaningful when TRUE. Not the same as lavaan's std.ov/std.lv, which re-parameterises the whole model on a standardised scale. Defaults to FALSE.

sn_fit_ngrid

Use control = inlavaan_control(n_grid = ), which gives the same fit.

sn_fit_logthresh

Use control = inlavaan_control(log_threshold = ), which gives the same fit.

sn_fit_temp

Has no effect. The skew-normal marginals are fitted with temperature 1.

sn_fit_sample

Logical. When TRUE (default), a parametric skew-normal is fitted to the posterior samples for covariance and defined parameters. When FALSE, these are summarised using kernel density estimation instead.

control

A list of tuning settings, made by inlavaan_control(), or a plain list with some of its names: the limits of the search for the posterior mode, of the VB correction and of the skew-normal scans, and the settings hessian, debug and add_priors. The defaults suit most fits. An unknown name gives an error. The controls of stats::nlminb() that control took up to INLAvaan 0.3.5, such as iter.max, still work, with a deprecation warning. See inlavaan_control().

verbose

Logical. With FALSE (default) the fit prints one line per stage. With TRUE it also prints the details of each stage of the fit on the internal scale: the start, the mode search, the VB correction and the marginals, with their checks. Use silent = TRUE to print nothing.

debug

Use control = inlavaan_control(debug = TRUE), which gives the same fit.

add_priors

Use control = inlavaan_control(add_priors = FALSE), which gives the same fit.

optim_method

Has no effect. The posterior mode is always found by stats::nlminb().

numerical_grad

Has no effect. The fit always uses the analytic gradient.

hessian_method

Use control = inlavaan_control(hessian = ), which gives the same fit.

cores

A positive whole number or NULL. The number of cores. Other values, such as 0, 2.5 or NA, give an error. With NULL (default), the scans of the skew-normal marginals follow future::plan(), which is serial unless a plan is set, and the LOO and the WAIC asked for in test run serially. With cores > 1, the scans run in parallel when the packages future and parallelly are installed, and serially otherwise. The LOO and the WAIC are then forked via parallel::mclapply() where that is safe, or run over a PSOCK cluster (separate R processes) inside IDE R sessions (RStudio, Positron) and on Windows. 1 is serial.

ppp_method

How the PPP of a two-level model scores the observed and the replicate data against the saturated model. "onestep" (default) takes one Fisher-scoring step from the moments of each posterior draw towards the saturated fit, and fits by EM where the step would leave the valid covariance matrices (with few clusters or a small between variance). "em" always fits the saturated model by EM, as blavaan does. Fits with missing = "ml" always use "em". Ignored for single-level models.

ppp_nsamp

The number of posterior draws, each with one replicate data set, that the PPP of a two-level model uses. Defaults to 250, and is capped at nsamp. Draws that cannot be scored are left out, with a warning. Ignored for single-level models.

marginal_scan

How the scan behind each skew-normal marginal is taken. "linear" (default) scans along a straight line through the mode, and adds a linear correction for the changing volume of the other parameters. "exact" computes that volume term exactly at each point of the scan. "laplace" maximises the log-posterior over the other parameters at each point of the scan, and takes the height and the volume there. "plain" adds no volume correction. On the Holzinger and Swineford and the Political Democracy models, "exact" and "laplace" take 10 to 25 times as long as "linear". Ignored with marginal_method = "gaussian", which has no scan.

silent

Logical. Print nothing at all, and muffle the warnings and messages raised during the fit? Default FALSE. verbose and silent cannot both be TRUE. Errors are still raised. Whether or not silent is TRUE, the texts of the warnings raised during the fit are recorded in the field warnings of get_inlavaan_internal().

...

Additional arguments to be passed to the lavaan model fitting function.

Value

An S4 object of class INLAvaan which is a subclass of the lavaan class.

Details

The agrowth() function is a wrapper for the more general inlavaan() function, using the following default arguments:

  • meanstructure = TRUE

  • int.ov.free = FALSE

  • int.lv.free = TRUE

  • auto.fix.first = TRUE (unless std.lv = TRUE)

  • auto.fix.single = TRUE

  • auto.var = TRUE

  • auto.cov.lv.x = TRUE

  • auto.efa = TRUE

  • auto.th = TRUE

  • auto.delta = TRUE

  • auto.cov.y = TRUE

See also

Typically, users will interact with the specific latent variable model functions instead, including acfa(), asem(), and agrowth().

Examples

# Linear growth model with a time-varying covariate
mod <- "
  # Intercept and slope with fixed coefficients
    i =~ 1*t1 + 1*t2 + 1*t3 + 1*t4
    s =~ 0*t1 + 1*t2 + 2*t3 + 3*t4

  # (Latent) regressions
    i ~ x1 + x2
    s ~ x1 + x2

  # Time-varying covariates
    t1 ~ c1
    t2 ~ c2
    t3 ~ c3
    t4 ~ c4
"
utils::data("Demo.growth", package = "lavaan")
str(Demo.growth)
#> 'data.frame':	400 obs. of  10 variables:
#>  $ t1: num  1.726 -1.984 0.32 0.777 0.449 ...
#>  $ t2: num  2.142 -4.401 -1.269 3.531 -0.773 ...
#>  $ t3: num  2.77 -6.02 1.56 3.14 -1.5 ...
#>  $ t4: num  2.516 -7.0296 2.8685 5.3637 0.0785 ...
#>  $ x1: num  -1.16 -1.75 0.92 2.36 -1.09 ...
#>  $ x2: num  0.174 -1.577 -0.142 0.708 -1.01 ...
#>  $ c1: num  -0.0277 -2.032 0.0524 0.0191 0.6524 ...
#>  $ c2: num  0.555 0.125 -1.258 0.647 0.731 ...

#>  $ c4: num  -1.0064 1.2293 -0.3273 -1.0324 -0.0275 ...

fit <- agrowth(mod, data = Demo.growth, nsamp = 100)
